- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.16 or lower) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 1–2% relative to prior high.
- If model forecast spikes sharply after a low, true price often lags and doesn’t reach forecast peak — cap forecast at 1–2% below prior 30d high.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.00 or +0.27), model often underestimates upward momentum — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently overestimates short-term mean reversion after strong moves — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for 3–7 day horizon if sentiment is flat or mildly negative.
- If sentiment turns positive after a prolonged negative streak (e.g., +0.27), model often fails to fully capture the rally — increase forecast by 1–2% for next 5–10 days.
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves when sentiment is mixed or trending downward — cap forecast at 1–2% below recent 14-day high unless sentiment is clearly bullish.
